sections.overview: The Komodo dragon is the world’s largest living lizard and is endemic to a few Indonesian islands.
sections.identification: Adults are large, heavy monitor lizards with a long tail, strong limbs and a forked tongue; juveniles are smaller and more vividly patterned.
sections.habitat: It uses tropical savanna, forest, scrub and other island habitats, from beaches to higher ridges.
sections.diet: It hunts vertebrates and also scavenges carcasses; prey size and diet change as it grows.
sections.behavior: It locates food chiefly by smell, sampling airborne scents with its long, forked tongue.
sections.reproduction: Females lay eggs; young dragons spend much of their early life in trees, where they are less exposed to larger conspecifics.
sections.ecology: As a large island predator, it shares its habitat with other monitor lizards but is distinguished by its exceptional size and restricted range.
sections.conservation: The IUCN lists it as Endangered; its small, fragmented island range and projected climate-related habitat loss are major concerns.
